business_problem: Innocens BV needed a faster, more reliable way to detect signs of late-onset sepsis in vulnerable newborns because NICU teams were relying on manual interpretation of many data sources and could miss critical changes for hours.
solution_summary: Innocens BV worked with IBM to turn a decade of neonatal intensive care data into an explainable clinical decision-support platform. Using IBM Watson Studio on IBM Cloud Pak for Data, the team trained machine learning models on monitoring signals, reports, diagnoses, and patient-record data from Antwerp University Hospital. The implementation was designed around three architectural pillars identified by the team: a predictive model, an interpretable user interface, and a robust edge-oriented architecture. Explainable AI features in Cloud Pak for Data were used to help caregivers understand why the models were flagging risk, while federated learning let the models evolve without moving raw patient data outside the hospital. Parameters could move through the cloud, but raw NICU data stayed on premises behind hospital firewalls, creating a privacy-preserving operating model for continuous sepsis monitoring.

data_flow: Monitoring signals, reports, diagnoses, and electronic patient-record data remain inside the hospital environment, Watson Studio models analyze the patterns through Cloud Pak for Data, and federated-learning parameters move in the cloud while clinicians receive explainable risk insight locally.
business_outcome: The Innocens platform gave clinicians a path to detect severe sepsis earlier, preserve patient-data locality, and build a reusable AI foundation for broader neonatal decision support.
